questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I just created a user on hybel and found a collective there who rented out a free room. I think it was easier because I'm Danish though. Non-scandinavians might have a more difficult time with it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Idk :)

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't remember

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could call or write to them. They answered very quickly

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Semi-successful. One course about preperation for masters assignmnent, I was not allowed to register for because I'm not a full masters student at UiO. But I liked that you were able to shop around.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
1. Register for a bunch of classes in the beginning. You can always drop the ones you don't like. It's not like in UCPH
2. Remember that if you're a masters student the courses might be build in blocks. Make sure to spread these blocks out, so you don't have to do 3 exams for difficult courses at the same time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took two bachelor courses (between authoritarianism and democracy in the post communist region + British politics and Institutions) and one masters course (Democracy: From theory to practice). I really liked the masters course and the post communist course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More or less the same. A bit more assignments during the semester perhaps?

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
STV2380 – Between Authoritarianism and Democracy in the Post-communist Region (Bachelor)
STV1560 – British Politics and institutions (Bachelor)
STV4105 – Democracy: From Theory to Practice (Master)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
STV4105 – Democracy: From Theory to Practice. Jonathan is amazing and hilarious.

I also really really enjoyed STV2380 – Between Authoritarianism and Democracy in the Post-communist Region.

questions.answer: I used a bunch of money on travel while there

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
When in Norway, you expect everything to be more expensive. This was not the case. The norwegian crown was extremely low while I was in Oslo, so many things were cheaper than expected.

Cheaper than expected: Housing, coffee, candy, transportation.
More expensive: Alcohol, vegetables, eating out, meat...

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A bunch! MANY sports associations and other associations.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Please go hiking!

Also! I was a vollunteer at the cafe, which meant I both met a bunch of nice people there AND got free coffee for the entire semester. Huge recommendation! If you're social science, volunteer at U1.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Lofoten!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Extremely easy. Norwegian and Danish culture is basically the same. AND THE NORWEGIANS LOVE DANES! So extremely easy to make friends.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be open. They really like chatting with danes. The people who are interested will find you as long as you're nice and outgoing:)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Alcohol-culture. They're more strict than in Denmark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Easy-goingness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared to spend money on trips!
Socialize with Norwegians!
Live in the center if possible.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: They're very well-organized. Don't hesitate to reach out for help.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people and self-developement

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I was surprised to find out, you had to pay to go to the doctor (not a large amount, but still)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
